leaders.notes: Took office as interim president Aug. 1, 1994, and was made permanent president in 1995, serving through 2003. Went on to lead Utah Valley State College (later University) 2003-2008, then served as Utah's higher-ed commissioner and later interim chancellor of UNC Wilmington.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.notes: 18th president; Ferris's longest-serving president after founder Woodbridge Ferris. Announced retirement in March 2021, effective June 2022; the University Center building was later named for him.
19th president, took office July 1, 2022 succeeding Eisler; first African American to lead Ferris State since its 1884 founding. Currently serving.

SAGE Publications founder and longtime Fielding trustee; stepped in as interim president starting Feb. 18, 1999 during a leadership transition, serving until Judith Kuipers was named president in 2000. Served nine years as president after leading UW-La Crosse for nearly a decade. Later served on Fresno State's College of Arts and Humanities advisory board; passed away in 2024.
Capped a 37-year career serving as president of five higher-education institutions; announced retirement in Nov. 2012, effective end of July 2013.

Began as acting president July 21, 2013 (promoted from within as Provost) and was confirmed permanent president that November. Became Fielding's longest-serving president; retired at contract's end Jan. 31, 2025 and rejoined the faculty.

leaders.notes: A Fielding alumnus and former Fielding Board of Trustees member; began as president Feb. 1, 2025, succeeding Katrina Rogers. Currently serving.

leaders.priorInstitution: State University System of Florida (Board of Regents)
leaders.notes: Founding president, appointed April 26, 1993; planned, shaped and launched Florida's 10th public university, welcoming its first student cohort in 1997. Retired May 1999.

Second president, July 1999 to January 2007; enrollment surged and the university secured over $175 million in private gifts under his tenure. Resigned after admitting to an extramarital affair with a faculty member; died in 2011.

Named interim president by the FGCU Board of Trustees following Merwin's January 2007 resignation; bridged the gap until Wilson Bradshaw's arrival in August 2007, then returned to his business-school deanship.
Third president, Aug. 25, 2007 to June 30, 2017; oversaw a 60% enrollment increase, new campus construction and FGCU's first doctoral program. FGCU's library was later named in his honor.

leaders.priorTitle: Chancellor Emeritus and Senior Fellow (previously Chancellor)
leaders.notes: Fourth president, July 2017 to 2023; navigated the university through the COVID-19 pandemic and launched the Water School in 2019. Stepped into a nonprofit leadership role upon leaving FGCU.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice President and Vice Provost for Strategy and Program Innovation
leaders.notes: Fifth president, selected May 4, 2023 and officially installed Jan. 2024; first woman and first immigrant to lead FGCU. Currently serving.

leaders.priorTitle: Dean, College of Arts and Sciences
leaders.notes: Became Gallaudet's first deaf president in March 1988, following the landmark 'Deaf President Now' student protests. Stepped down Dec. 31, 2006 as the university's longest-serving modern president.

leaders.priorInstitution: National Technical Institute for the Deaf, Rochester Institute of Technology
leaders.notes: Ninth president, Jan. 1, 2007 to Dec. 31, 2009; earlier served as a Gallaudet vice president and professor in the 1970s-80s before returning as its leader.

leaders.priorInstitution: National Technical Institute for the Deaf, Rochester Institute of Technology
leaders.notes: Tenth president, Jan. 1, 2010 to Dec. 31, 2015; previously led NTID at RIT as dean and vice president. Succeeded by Roberta Cordano.

Eleventh president, officially installed Sept. 30, 2016; previously a Minnesota assistant attorney general and charter-school founder. Named a USA Today 2023 Women of the Year honoree. Currently serving.
